answer: A stake-bonded reputation works like basalt bedrock: each agent must lock a deposit that is slashed if it misbehaves, so spinning up fake identities costs real money. Reputation then accrues only from verified work, like layers of onyx laid down over time, and a raven-style peer audit randomly samples agents to check their claims. An attacker must fund every fake identity and survive audits, so the cost of a Sybil swarm grows faster than its influence.
